messages.subject: Re: rjava problem posted on rosada
messages.body_plain:
Joe,

yes, rJava uses a custom class loader in order to support custom  
search paths for class files and libraries. However, it's passing a  
request to load resources down to the boot loader and also it looks up  
resources in the JAR files on the class path as well as directories on  
the class path. If you set verbose to anything >0 (e.g. via  
RJavaClassLoader.setDebug(1)), you'll get some messages that may help  
you identify the problem. If I am to help you, you'll have to be more  
specific what code exactly you use to locate the resource and what is  
exactly your layout.

Cheers,
Simon

information from the output below)

Cheers,
Simon

rJava and JavaGD are packages that JGR depends on. Since you installed

messages.subject: JGR problems
messages.body_plain:
Dear JGR Developers!

I have recently updated to JGR 1.5 (I know, Iknow...) and encountered
some problems, that have not occurred in the previous versions. These
may be caused by the reimplementation of the editor or the new default
look&feel...

1. unsolicited "popup":
I use JGR with a hungarian keyboard: that means that certain
characters I can only invoke with AltGr (right Alt) keycombinations
(e.g. [: AltGr+F, ]: AltGr+G, @: AltGr+V, }: AltGr+N, etc.) Besides
producing the requested character all these combos have the
side-effect of opening unwanted popup windows (e.g. AltGr+F and
AltGr+G both invoke the "Find" window) what is _really_ very annoying.
It seems that the  AltGr+... combos are interpreted as if they were
CTRL+... by java (or JGR itself?).

2. fontsize bug:
Sometimes the cursor position gets out of synchron with the visible
output in the editor. (See "fontsize_bug.jpg", where the cursor _is_
currently at the end of line (moving it one character to the right
puts it at the start of the next line, note also the small boxlet
indicating the pair of the trailing parenthesis in the same line)).
Unfortunately I cannot give step-by-step instructions how to reproduce
this bug, but it occurs from time to time if I change the font size
within the editor several times (and eventually do some cursor moving
and typing in between)

3. lack of some standard keybindings:
This is a bug/feature that is very annoying for me personally, because
I am very much accustomed to the traditional keybindings of SHIFT+DEL
(cut), CTRL+INS (copy) and SHIFT+INS (paste) available almost
everywhere in  both the windows and the unix/linux world. These combos
have been working as wished (at least under windows) under the
previous versions of JGR, but do not work any more with 1.5. Although
I know of the also standard alternatives (ctrl+x,c,v), the original
CUA (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_User_Access) bindings would
also be useful for some (many) users, especially for the left-handed
(http://forums.networkautomation.com/forum/messageview.cfm?catid=4&threadid=3581&enterthread=y)

4. overprint bug:
I like the new line numbers in the editor window, probably coming from
jedit very much, although I would like to draw your attention to a
small problem of visual representation (see
"linenumber_overprint_bug.jpg"). This happens, if the visible area is
scrolled to the right in the editor. BTW, is there a way for wrapping
long lines automatically?

I hope that these problems are not really difficult to fix, and I will
be able to use  the current version without any pain. I am sorry if I
am at the wrong forum, and the solution would be to change some
general java settings -- please forgive my ignorance, and point me to
the right direction in this case... (However, I have been googling
extensively e.g. to fing a way to change the L&F for JGR to the
windows L&F, to see whether this could solve any of my problems... --
without success.)

JGR has been my favourite R GUI for almost two years, and many thanks
for developing and maintaining of this nice and very useful tool!
Bálint

--

messages.subject: rJava Jar file loading performance
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

We have about 40 MB of class files packaged into about a dozen jars.  When 
running our code through rJava, we noticed a dramatic slowdown.  Therefore 
I ran a small experiment.  I extracted all of our classes directly to the 
filesystem and also made a single jar with all classes.  I then measured 
the speed it took to run a specific section of our code.  In the jar file 
it took approximately 70 seconds.  When using the fully extracted classes 
it took just over 2 seconds.  This leads me to think there are some 
performance problems with the RJavaClassLoader when class files are in 
jars.  What can we do?

Regards,
Dylan

messages.subject: Re: JGR and site-library
messages.body_plain:
On Feb 26, 2008, at 4:34 AM, Erich Neuwirth wrote:

> I am using JGR 1.5-8 on Windows XP with R 2.6.2.
> I keep all the additional packages in site-library instead of library.
> R honors this and finds the packages without any problems.
> When I start JGR, however, it tells me that it needs to download
> packages, does it, and then exits with an error message.
> Next time started it does the same thing.
> Moving JGR, rJava, JavaGD and iplots from site-library to library
> immediately solves the problem.
>
> Should this be fixed in JGR?
> Can it be solved temporarily by setting an environment variable?
>

On unix you can set R_LIBS accordingly. When run the first time, JGR  
saves this setting to its preference file, so you only need to specify  
it once.
On Windows, you have no choice, because the check is performed based  
on the registry setting of R before the preference file is read. How  
do you set a non-standard location? Clearly .Rprofile is not an  
option, because that requires a running R already.
I could add an option such that you could add let's say a registry key  
to override the path that JGR is using, but I'm not sure how  
compatible that would be ...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
On Feb 26, 2008, at 9:57 AM, Dylan_Wilson at bd.com wrote:

>
> Hi,
>
> We have about 40 MB of class files packaged into about a dozen  
> jars.  When running our code through rJava, we noticed a dramatic  
> slowdown.  Therefore I ran a small experiment.  I extracted all of  
> our classes directly to the filesystem and also made a single jar  
> with all classes.  I then measured the speed it took to run a  
> specific section of our code.  In the jar file it took approximately  
> 70 seconds.  When using the fully extracted classes it took just  
> over 2 seconds.  This leads me to think there are some performance  
> problems with the RJavaClassLoader when class files are in jars.   
> What can we do?
>

Extract the files. It's much faster to access plain files than to  
unpack them one by one.
I'm not sure what Sun is doing, but anything short of unpacking all  
files is probably very inefficient. rJava class loader first looks for  
plain files and if they cannot be found, it simply extracts the files  
on demand which is efficient when using a handful class files from  
large JAR files, but it will quickly become inefficient with very  
complex projects that use many files. Patches for a faster loaded are  
always welcome.

Cheers,
Simon
